t:
(a) Preservation of Leave.—Notwithstanding section 701(b) of title 10, United States Code, any member of the Coast Guard 
who served on active duty for a continuous period of 30 days, who was assigned to duty or otherwise detailed in support of units or operations in the Eighth Coast Guard District area of responsibility for activities to mitigate the consequences of, or assist in the recovery from, Hurricane Katrina during the period beginning on August 28, 2005, and ending on January 1, 2006, and who would have otherwise lost any accumulated leave in excess of 60 days as a consequence of such assignment, is authorized to retain an accumulated total of up to 120 days of leave. 
    (b) Excess Leave.—Leave in excess of 60 days accumulated under subsection (a) shall be lost unless used by the member before the commencement of the second fiscal year following the fiscal year in which the assignment commences, or in the case of a Reserve member, the year in which the period of active service is completed.

fable.w: This section only lets Coast Guard members who supported Hurricane Katrina response retain accumulated leave beyond the usual limit, and sets when that excess leave expires. The only tempting hook is that it concerns people and disaster recovery, but it addresses federal personnel benefits alone. It contains no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: any member of the Coast Guard

opus.w: This section only lets Coast Guard members who served in the Hurricane Katrina response keep up to 120 days of accumulated leave, and sets when the extra leave is lost. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and the section creates no hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The Katrina relief context might suggest working with state or local partners, but the text deals only with leave for federal service members.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines leave entitlements for Coast Guard members who served on active duty. Since Coast Guard members on active duty are federal employees, this is an internal personnel matter regarding benefits, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with parties outside the government. It does not involve public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: any member of the Coast Guard who served on active duty... is authorized to retain an accumulated total of up to 120 days of leave.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute mentions "members of the Coast Guard" and "Reserve members," it involves people outside the federal government. However, Coast Guard members on active duty are federal employees. The statute merely defines their leave entitlements, which is an internal personnel matter, not a process for outside participation in a federal decision.
